newsitem.title: USA: USDA says cooks should use thermometer in hamburger.
newsitem.headline: USDA says cooks should use thermometer in hamburger.

text.p: In a food safety warning at the start of the summer cookout season, the U.S. Agriculture Department Tuesday said consumers should use a thermometer to cook hamburger because new research shows the color of meat is not a reliable gauge of doneness.

USDA's Food Safety and Inspection Service (FSIS) said to be safe from harmful bacteria such as E.coli 0157.H7, which struck in fast-food restaurant hamburgers in 1993 in the Pacific Northwest making hundreds sick and killing four children, ground beef must be cooked to 160 degrees Fahrenheit.

New research shows some ground meat may turn prematurely brown before hitting the safe cooking temperature. At the same time, other hamburger patties stay pink when cooked to 160 degrees Fahrenheit or above, the department said.

"In the face of this new research and seemingly conflicting data and viewpoints, the FSIS alerts consumers that the color of meat is no longer considered a reliable indicator of ground beef safety," said Thomas Billy, head of the food safety arm.
"A meat thermometer is the most reliable way to reduce the risk of foodborne illness," he said.
Billy said FSIS would hold a public meeting in the near future to call for additional research and to discuss all the issues surrounding the safe cooking of hamburger.
